question: Is GTDB-Tk cost fixed per run or linear in the genomes it processes?
why_it_mattered: The two models differed by 94x at a million genomes (48 vs 4,500 CPU-h) and the cost projection assumed the favourable one. Our two pipeline runs differed by only 4.6% in the genomes GTDB-Tk actually sees, which cannot separate the models.
method: gtdbtk classify_wf with the pipeline module flags (--cpus 8, --pplacer_cpus 1, --min_perc_aa 10, --skip_ani_screen, --scratch_dir), single shard, on 8 and then 64 Erwiniaceae genomes drawn in a fixed order from the BGC-positive set. 2026-09-18.

fit.verdict: LINEAR. The fixed cost is real (23.2 CPU-min) but per-genome cost dominates above roughly 40 genomes.

projection_cpu_hours.basis: 0.630 x 104,785 + 23.2 x 21 shards = 66,511 CPU-min = 1,108 CPU-h. The population is BGC-POSITIVE GENOMES at the controlled Erwiniaceae pair's measured rate: 300 of 2,863 genomes = 10.48%, so ~104,800 at a million. GTDB-Tk sees only these (gtdbtk_bgc_genomes_only), not the 10,504 CPU-h a million genomes would cost if all were placed.
projection_cpu_hours.supersedes_121000: An earlier version of this file gave 1,271 CPU-h at '~121,000 BGC-positive genomes'. 121,000 is NOT a genome count. It is the BGC count: 333 regions / 2,758 genomes on the 2026-08 Erwiniaceae benchmark = 120,740 at a million. That run's BGC-POSITIVE GENOME count was 298 / 2,758 = 108,049. So a count of clusters was substituted for a count of genomes, overstating GTDB-Tk by ~15%. The figure is correct for BiG-SCAPE, which does consume BGCs, and that is probably how it migrated. Same species of error as the realtime x cpus / realtime x %cpu mix-up: a quantity used where a different quantity belongs. State the POPULATION as well as the rate.
projection_cpu_hours.per_shard_wall_is_population_independent: A full 5,000-genome shard costs 0.630 x 5,000 + 23.2 = 3,173 CPU-min = 52.9 h, whatever the total. So the wall-clock figure (~53 h) does not move when the population is corrected; only the CPU-h total and the shard count do (24 -> 21).

consequences: The cost model assumed 48 CPU-h for GTDB-Tk. The measured figure is ~1,108 CPU-h at the corrected population. Note the '22,868 -> 24,100 CPU-h' total this line used to quote is itself superseded twice over -- see the Correction box in docs/manuscript/index.html section 2.6; the current projection is 15,330 unscreened / 4,946 screened on realtime x %cpu.
Sharding is cheap insurance after all: each shard re-pays only the 23.2 CPU-min intercept, so 20 shards add ~7.7 CPU-h to ~1,271 - about 0.6%.
Peak memory was 55.7 and 56.3 GB at N=8 and N=64, i.e. set by the reference data rather than by genome count - and close enough to this box's 56 GB that the measurement may be memory-bound.
caveats: Two points, both far below the 5,000-genome default shard size; the slope is assumed constant between them and is not verified at shard scale.
The 0.630 slope rests on two points (N=8, N=64), both far below the 5,000-genome shard size, and is unverified at shard scale. It is the dominant term in the 1,108 CPU-h figure.
